cards.title: The Heat Exchange
cards.tagline: A net-zero learning hub on the Students' Car Park, NTU Clifton

cards.title: What is it?
cards.text: A two-storey timber learning hub: a cafe and entrance atrium, a flexible teaching hall, a makerspace, a library and study pods, an edge server room and a cycle hub, all on what is now a car park.

cards.title: Where
cards.text: Students' Car Park, Clifton Campus, Nottingham NG11 8NS. {lat}° N, {lon}° {lon_dir}. Ground floor {ffl} m above sea level.

cards.title: Peek inside
cards.text: Lift any wall straight up out of its slot to see the site model. All four are the same size; the label on the hidden strip says which side each one belongs on.
Every number on these walls comes from the same model as the building behind them.

cards.title: Energy
cards.tagline: Why it's called The Heat Exchange

cards.title: Where the heat comes from
steps: {server_racks} server racks run day and night at about {server_kw} kW each
Rear-door heat exchangers catch their waste heat in water
A water-source heat pump lifts it to 45-55 °C
A thermal store holds it until the rooms need it
MVHR keeps 85-90% of the heat in the stale air it swaps for fresh

cards.title: Computers that heat the building
cards.text: Most buildings pay to throw server heat away. Here the edge server room is the boiler: about {server_heat_mwh} MWh a year of heat that would otherwise be wasted.

cards.title: Sun on the roof
cards.text: {pv_modules} panels ({pv_kwp} kWp) face south at {pv_tilt}° on the sawtooth roof, with more on carports over the parking that stays. A battery keeps midday sun for the evening.

cards.title: Light only where it's needed
cards.text: {led_panels} LED panels and {light_sensors} occupancy + daylight sensors use about {lighting_design_kwh} kWh a year, against {lighting_baseline_kwh} kWh for old fluorescent tubes left on.

cards.title: Fresh air, measured
cards.text: {iaq_sensors} sensors track CO₂, temperature and humidity in every room, so ventilation runs when people are there, not by the clock.

cards.title: Shade that knows the seasons
cards.text: Noon sun is {sun_june}° high in June but {sun_december}° in December, so the {overhang_m} m overhang shades {shade_june} m of the glass below it in summer but only {shade_december} m in winter.

cards.title: The building
cards.tagline: {length_m} x {depth_m} m, {storeys} storeys, {height_m} m to the roof peaks

cards.title: Built from timber
cards.text: Cross-laminated timber walls and floors lock up carbon instead of emitting it. The outer wall is 360 mm: 100 mm CLT, 220 mm wood-fibre insulation and 40 mm cladding.

cards.title: A sawtooth roof
cards.text: Each tooth carries solar panels on its south slope and glass on its north face, bringing soft, glare-free daylight deep into the first floor.

cards.title: Glass where it helps
cards.text: Glazing is {wwr_s}% of the south wall and {wwr_w}% of the west, but just {wwr_e}% east and {wwr_n}% north. {volume_m3} m³ heated inside {envelope_m2} m² of envelope.

cards.title: Site & people
cards.tagline: A car park that becomes a landscape

cards.title: Greener ground
cards.text: Meadow, a rain garden and a pond replace tarmac, with new paths across the site. The parking that stays sits under solar carports.

cards.title: Arrive by bike
cards.text: The cycle hub has {bike_spaces} spaces in two-tier racks, e-bike charging lockers, showers and changing rooms, all under a living green roof.

cards.title: Rain that flushes
cards.text: Rainwater from the roofs is stored and pumped to flush dual-flush WCs, and a refill station cuts plastic bottles.

cards.title: A building that teaches
cards.text: The makerspace has a laser cutter and 3D printers, and the Smart Building Control Room shows the building's live energy data to students.

cards.title: UN Sustainable Development Goals
cards.text: Mainly 7 clean energy, 9 innovation, 12 responsible consumption and 13 climate action; also 4 quality education and 11 sustainable cities.

cards.title: How we made this model
steps: Real ground heights from Environment Agency LiDAR, plus OpenStreetMap
One Python model of the building drives every output
Printed on NTU's Bambu printers: {print_hours} h and {print_grams} g of PLA
A walk-through web twin and a Google Earth model
These walls, laser-engraved from the same files

cards.title: Honest numbers
cards.text: Fit-out is costed at about £{fitout_k}k from indicative prices. Plant such as the heat pump and battery is still to be sized by an energy model.
